label: diplazioid
definition: A positional quality inhering in a pair of sori by virtue of their lying back to back along both sides of the same vein, opening in opposite directions.
reason: A real fern term for how sori sit, as in Diplazium. No PATO or FLOPO term covers it. It is used only on sori.
'Discernible' means visible, read like the earlier rule 'distinct' = conspicuous. 'Hardly' and 'slightly' are degree words and are handled as modifiers.
'Transverse veins very distinctive' means clearly visible, the same reading as the rule for 'distinct'. 'Terminal buds distinctive' may mean 'typical of the taxon', so this is less certain.
A fruit that is dorsally compressed (as in Apiaceae) is flattened from back to front, which is PATO dorso-ventrally flattened.
Two values joined into one word. 'Doubly' (teeth bearing smaller teeth) has no term, and the continuum between the two values carries most of the meaning.
Unclear: it could mean folded (conduplicate) or doubled, and the leaf example is a cut-off piece of text. Too vague without its context.
Two existing values joined in one word, like 'linear-lanceolate'.
A length compared with another part (petal). This is the equality pattern, not a term.
A range between two existing FLOPO values.
Two comparisons with the leaves given as alternatives: 'as long as' and 'longer than'.
A pinna base that is equally sided is symmetrical, the opposite of an inequilateral base.
Here it states that thickness is the same along the stem or among the branches. That is a comparison, and a term for it would be doubtful. PATO has only 'irregular thickness' as the opposite.
Two existing margin values joined in one word.
Probably means 'without a sheath', but 'sheath' was rejected earlier as a part that needs its organ. On petal segments the meaning is unclear.

label: explosively dehiscent
definition: A dehiscent quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's opening suddenly and forcibly at maturity so that its seeds are thrown out.
reason: A known kind of fruit opening (Impatiens, many legumes), next to septicidal, loculicidal and poricidal, which were already added under dehiscent.
Two existing shape values joined in one word. PATO lists falcate as a synonym of falciform.
A feeble stem is weak, and 'weak' is a synonym of PATO decreased strength. Feeble veins mean inconspicuous, so the rule is limited to stems and branches.
A loose count of fruits, like 'few-flowered'.
Two existing shape values joined in one word.
Two existing shape values joined in one word.
A testa that is reticulate has a network pattern. 'Finely' says how fine the network is and is a modifier.
Vague and means different things: wood grain versus fine roots. No clear quality.
Same as the existing rule for 'veined'. 'Finely' is a modifier.
A growth stage of the part, not a quality. It is already in config/flora_context_words.tsv.
Fusoid means spindle-shaped, which is PATO fusiform: wide in the middle and tapering at both ends.
Fuzz on seeds (as in cotton) is a cover of short hairs, so the seed is hairy.
A misspelling of glabrescent.
Flowers in glomerules are in dense clusters. PATO aggregated has 'clustered' as a synonym. FLOPO capitate (a single head) would say too much.
Same as the existing rule for 'narrowing'.

label: graduated
definition: An unequal quality inhering in a series of overlapping structures of the same kind by virtue of its members increasing step by step in length from the outermost to the innermost.
reason: A common term for overlapping bracts, phyllaries and sepals. It is a more specific kind of unequal that no existing term covers.
